Definition: strengthened from G4154; to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown):--choke, take by the throat.
BiblicalUsage: Pnigo means to choke, to strangle. The seed among thorns was choked in Matthew 13:7, and the swine ran violently into the sea and were choked in Mark 5:13. The unforgiving servant took his fellow by the throat in Matthew 18:28 — the same word, choking a brother over a debt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe thorns choke seed, swine choke in the sea, and an unforgiving hand chokes a brother — and all three are the same sin.
